column1: # Employee Scheduling Demand Requirements Template
# PURPOSE:
#   This CSV specifies HOW MANY people are needed for each day/shift/team combination.
#   The algorithm uses these requirements to generate the schedule.
# REQUIRED COLUMNS:
#   date           - Date in YYYY-MM-DD format (ISO 8601)
#   shift          - Shift code (must match a shift defined in problem.json shifts array)
#   team           - Team/competency code (see note below about this column)
#   minimum        - Minimum people required (hard constraint - MUST be satisfied)
#   ideal          - Ideal number of people (soft target - algorithm tries to reach this)
#   estimated      - Estimated demand (used for KPI analysis after schedule generation)
# IMPORTANT NOTE ABOUT THE "team" COLUMN:
#   The "team" column is semantically flexible depending on your employee model:
#   - If using TEAM MODEL (employees.model="team"):
#     → This column contains TEAM CODES from organizationalUnits.teams[]
#     → Example: "TeamA"
#   - If using COMPETENCY MODEL (employees.model="competency"):
#     → This column contains COMPETENCY CODES from organizationalUnits.competencies[].code
#     → Example: "EG"
# VALIDATION RULES:
#   1. All dates must be within temporalScope.targetPeriod in problem.json
#   2. All shift codes must exist in demand.shifts[].code in problem.json
#   3. All team/competency codes must exist in organizationalUnits.teams[] or
#      organizationalUnits.competencies[].code in problem.json
#   4. Values must satisfy: minimum <= estimated <= ideal
#   5. No duplicate rows (same date/shift/team combination)
# FORMAT REQUIREMENTS:
#   - Dates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g.
#   - All numeric values must be non-negative integers
#   - One row per day/shift/team combination
#   - No empty values
# COVERAGE LOGIC:
#   - minimum: Hard constraint - schedule MUST have at least this many people
#   - ideal: Soft constraint - algorithm tries to assign this many (may assign less if needed)
#   - estimated: Not used by algorithm
# HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE:
#   1. Copy this file and rename it (e.g.
#   2. Delete all comment lines (lines starting with #)
#   3. Keep the header row (date
#   4. Add your coverage requirements - one row per day/shift/team
#   5. Validate using: Check that all shifts exist
# EXAMPLES:
#   For a simple 2-team
#date
# COMMON PATTERNS:
#   - Weekdays need more staff: increase minimum/ideal on Mon-Fri
#   - Special events: increase ideal for specific dates
#   - Reduced hours (weekends/holidays): fewer shifts or lower minimum
# TIPS FOR LARGE PROBLEMS (365 days):
#   - Use Excel/LibreOffice to generate the CSV with formulas
#   - Use WEEKDAY() function to set different values for weekdays vs weekends
#   - Use IF() statements for holidays/special events
#   - Copy-paste for repetitive patterns
